payload.proof_nl:
Let A and B be finite sets, and suppose there exists an injective function f : A -> B. We must prove |A| <= |B|.

Because A and B are finite, there exist natural numbers n and m such that |A| = n and |B| = m. We will show n <= m.

Consider the image f(A) = {f(a) : a in A} subseteq B. Since f is injective, the map f regarded as a function from A onto f(A) is bijective: it is surjective onto f(A) by definition of image, and it is injective by hypothesis. Therefore A and f(A) have the same cardinality, so
|A| = |f(A)|.

Now f(A) is a subset of B. Since B is finite, every subset of B has cardinality at most that of B. Hence
|f(A)| <= |B|.

Combining the two equalities/inequalities gives
|A| = |f(A)| <= |B|,
so |A| <= |B|, as required.

This proves that for all finite sets A and B, if there exists an injective function f : A -> B, then |A| <= |B|.
payload.role_in_assembly: Converts the injective map on finite Kunz sets into the desired inequality of their cardinalities.

payload.statement_nl: Let A and B be finite sets. If there exists an injective function f from A to B, then the cardinality of A is less than or equal to the cardinality of B.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly shows that an injective map A → B induces a bijection between A and its image f(A), yielding |A| = |f(A)|.
The proof correctly uses the standard finite-set fact that any subset of a finite set has cardinality at most that of the ambient set.
There is no semantic drift: the proof addresses exactly the stated lemma and supports the root theorem's counting-inequality step.

result_payload.reason: The proof is a standard and complete argument: restrict the injective map to its image to obtain a bijection A ≃ f(A), deduce |A| = |f(A)|, then use finiteness of B and inclusion f(A) ⊆ B to conclude |f(A)| ≤ |B|. This matches the lemma statement exactly and aligns with the intended role of converting an injection into a cardinality inequality.
